correctness.rationale: For each tangent-normal angular gap, the support-maximizing vertex is the intersection of the two tangent lines, giving the exact cosine-over-cosine support formula. Uniform-angle integration yields the closed-form width survival function. Its differentiated branches have positive, isolated one-sided square-root blow-ups at secant thresholds, so the threshold locations and amplitudes recover the distinct gaps and multiplicities. Essential minimum width identifies the inradius; dihedral orbit counting is exhaustive because the complete cyclic normal data give congruence. Analytic proof covers all m>=2, all strictly positive gaps, repetitions and threshold equalities. Bundled independent vertex-based finite checks returned VERIFY_OK for 300 checks, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Direction-unlabelled projection-length laws arise naturally in geometric tomography. This result identifies exactly the information retained in a full natural class of circumscribed centrally symmetric polygons: full inradius/gap-multiset recovery and exact loss of cyclic order, including the first ambiguity at eight sides and the generic fiber size (m-1)!/2 for every side count. This is an all-parameter structural inverse theorem rather than isolated computation, a change of variable or the already known unrestricted convex-body nonuniqueness example.
